timeline_reviews.summary: Transport stream accounted for manifest coverage; no projected semantic ledger events.
Serial parent timeline reviewed; it probes and writes modules sequentially with no delegation before timeout.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the Python source as `markdown.markdown(args.a, extensions=[extra])` with `--a` and `--b` required, ESM `.mjs` output, local-only modules, and `/output/test2.mjs` as final entry.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It chose broad concurrent behavior discovery via a workflow of feature-specific probe agents while the parent owned library implementation and final delivery.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a substantial `/output/lib/core` module tree and an argparse helper, reflecting a from-scratch markdown renderer attempt.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration never reached the required root entry; artifact validation listed only library files and no `test2.mjs`.
parallel.verification: Verification was dominated by delegated executable probes and workflow specs, but the killed workflow and missing entry left no evaluator-aligned end-to-end Node check.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out with a killed workflow, no retry budget, no `test2.mjs`, and official result 0/70.

serial.requirements: The serial run worked from the same prompt, read/probed the executable, and recognized required `--a`/`--b` CLI behavior and Python-Markdown extra output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With delegation disabled, one actor owned probing, implementation, file writes, and eventual delivery.
serial.implementation: It wrote a `/output/lib/md` module tree with parser, serializer, registry, preprocessor, and utility pieces.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It also did not create the required root `test2.mjs`, so artifact validation could not run the implementation.
serial.verification: It ran local executable probes and sample behavior checks inside the single trajectory, but did not complete final evaluator-aligned validation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process timed out with no subagents, no workflow child tokens, no `test2.mjs`, and official result 0/70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized Node.js ESM, `.mjs` suffixes, manual CLI parsing, Python-Markdown extra behavior, zero external dependencies, and `/output` delivery requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Worked from the same prompt and recognized the same source behavior: `--a` is rendered with Python-Markdown extra while `--b` is required but ignored.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference at prompt level; both ultimately missed the required root `test2.mjs` deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Split behavior discovery across a workflow with per-feature probe agents while the parent kept writing library modules in parallel.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Used one sequential actor: inspect dataset, probe executable behavior, then implement modules directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed broadly across many child probes; serial retained one owner and no delegated child work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs were feature-specific and specified probe outputs, corpora, and exact-byte behavior, but children shared generic temporary probe conventions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No inter-agent handoff or cross-agent interface existed; the same actor held prompt, probe observations, and implementation state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added child interface and temp-artifact coordination boundaries; serial avoided those handoff and temporary-path boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implemented a larger `/output/lib/core/*` structure plus CLI argparse helper, but did not place the required top-level entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Implemented `/output/lib/md/*` modules for parser pieces and utilities, also without the required top-level entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The module tree names and implementation organization differed, but the delivered artifacts shared the same missing-entry failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow reached a killed state with child retries and no returned aggregate result usable for final closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; local command results were immediately visible in the single trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unresolved workflow lifecycle; serial had no join or child-result retrieval boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children shared `/tmp` probe names and several detected another live agent in that namespace, requiring namespacing and reruns.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used local probe scripts and module writes without concurrent temp-file competition or shared workspace collisions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced shared-environment contamination around probes; serial only had ordinary sequential filesystem state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel generated many feature probes and some specs, but no final integrated Node entry was available for evaluator-aligned acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran executable probes and sample comparisons while implementing, but also had no final `test2.mjs` for official acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent verification effort in delegated probes; serial kept probes local. Neither reached whole-task delivered verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Timed out after 2399.609 seconds with workflow children consuming 2,456,168 child tokens and the workflow killed after stalls and a 429.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Timed out after 2399.696 seconds with workflows disabled, no child tokens, and no delivered entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the same wall-clock budget, but parallel also spent substantial budget on child fan-out and retries.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both evaluations completed and both failed 0/70 because the expected entry `test2.mjs` was absent from the collected artifact. The concrete task-solving difference is process shape, not result status: parallel spent large budget on a wide child-probe workflow plus parent implementation, while serial stayed sequential and still failed to deliver the entry file.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out, stalled retries, and API-pressure consumed budget while final entry assembly remained unfinished.
Shared `/tmp` probe artifacts forced child namespacing and reruns, adding avoidable parallel-only process cost.
serial_contributors: Serial control had no delegation or shared child workflow overhead but still timed out before writing `test2.mjs`.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel organized source under `lib/core` plus `lib/cli`; serial organized source under `lib/md`.
Both module trees were incomplete as deliverables because neither included the required root executable entry.
evaluator_effects: Artifact validation failed both runs on the same missing expected entry before behavior-specific testcase success was possible.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained labels describe adverse parallel-side process costs only
